module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 23

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture23

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 23](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, `b(G) ≥ ⌊α(G) + dist_avg(M) / 2⌋`, where `b(G)` is
the size of a largest induced bipartite subgraph, `α(G)` is the independence number,
`M` is the set of maximum-degree vertices, and `dist_avg(M)` is the average distance
between distinct vertices of `M`.

This conjecture is false; there is a counterexample with `b(G) = 19`, `α(G) = 15`,
and `dist_avg(M) = 10`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture23 : answer(False) ↔
  ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected),
    let M : Set α := {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}
    ⌊(G.indepNum : ℝ) + distAvgSet G M / 2⌋ ≤ (b G : ℝ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The invariant `b G` is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ b G := Nat.cast_nonneg _

/-- In `K₃`, the max degree is 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).maxDegree = 2 := by decide

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture23

reformulations.difference: Lean adds a Nontrivial vertex-type hypothesis and filters the average by distinct endpoints, whereas the source says connected graph and averages nonzero distances between maximum-degree vertices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a connected graph, G.dist u v = 0 iff u = v, so the two filters select exactly the same pairs. The omitted singleton graph satisfies the inequality automatically: distAvgSet is zero and the bound reduces to the independence number being at most the largest induced bipartite subgraph order. Every independent set induces a bipartite graph. The zero convention when M is a singleton likewise adds only automatic cases. The universal-statement equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/boundaries.lean as Review23.literal_source_universal_iff_current, without using the conjecture theorem.

review.notes: The theorem and both sanity checks are faithful. The source marks Conjecture 23 false and gives b = 19, independence number = 15, and average distance = 10, agreeing with answer(False), research solved, and the docstring. Lean experiments checked the definitions, empty/singleton averages, small complete graphs, and the harmless boundary restrictions. The live source was unavailable, so archived copies of the author's pages and definitions were used.
